text:
A: Hello. Yeah, I can hear you. Can you hear me?
B: Yes, yes, I can hear you. Hello! I'm Marites.
A: Tomasz. Nice to meet you.
B: Nice to meet you too. Sorry, my phone is a bit, erm, it's leaning on the rice cooker. Hehe.
A: Is fine. Is good picture, yeah.
B: Did you do the puzzle one before? The shapes?
A: Yeah. Er, I don't think I did very well, to be honest. I was going too fast at the end.
B: Oh my God, me too. I did the first ones okay and then the last ones I just guess. I'm not good with that kind of thing.
A: No, me neither. I'm better with real things, you know. Measuring and that.
B: What do you do?
A: I fit kitchens. Carpenter, kitchen fitter. For a small company in Basingstoke. I go to people's houses, take old kitchen out, put new one in. Worktops, doors, everything.
B: Oh, that's nice. That's hard work, no?
A: Yeah. Is okay. My knees don't like it so much now. What about you?
B: I'm a carer. Erm, home care, so I go to the old people in their houses, help them wash, get dressed, make their breakfast, check they take the medicine. Four days a week, around Croydon. Lots of buses. The 250 is always late, so I'm always running, to be honest.
A: Ah, same like me with the M3 in the morning. Every day is traffic.
B: Is it? You drive?
A: Yeah, I have the van. The door is broken a bit, the sliding one. It sticks. I keep saying I will fix it. Six months now.
B: Hehe. Like my plants, I keep saying I will water them.
A: Yeah.
B: You sound, erm, sorry, where are you from originally?
A: Poland. South-east, near Rzeszów. I came here in 2006. And you?
B: Philippines. Pampanga. I came in 2009, for a care home in Surrey first. Now I'm in London.
A: So we both came same time, almost.
B: Yeah! Do you go back home?
A: Most summers, yeah, two weeks. My mum is there, my sister. My mum lives alone now, so.
B: Oh. My parents also, they're still in Pampanga. I go every two or three years, when we can afford the flight. It's very expensive now. My dad is not so well, so I worry, you know. Every day I'm on Messenger with my sister asking, how is he, how is he.
A: Yeah. Is difficult. I speak to my mum every Sunday on video. She won't come here, she says is too cold.
B: Hehe, my mum also says that! Too cold, too grey.
A: Is true, to be fair.
B: You have children?
A: One. Oliver, he's ten. He plays football on Saturday morning, so I'm standing there in the cold.
B: Oh my God, same! Rafael is nine. Saturday football. I don't watch, I just chat with the other mums. He gets cross with me, he says, Mummy, you didn't see my goal.
A: Ha. Oliver says the same. I'm looking at phone.
B: And do you, erm, I saw in your picture there's a lot of things on the fridge also.
A: Yeah, is his drawing. And menu for the takeaway. My wife puts everything on fridge. Your fridge too, I think, I saw you have Santo Niño on top?
B: Yes! You know Santo Niño?
A: I'm Catholic too, so. Not the same, but I know. We go to Polish Mass in Reading sometimes. Christmas, Easter, always.
B: Oh, that's nice. I go every Sunday, but I'm always late. Always. The priest knows me now.
A: Ha. Better late than not going, my mum would say.
B: Exactly. That's what I tell myself, hehe. Erm, what else... do you cook Polish food at home?
A: At weekend, yeah. My wife is English, so she cooks in the week. I make bigos in winter. Pierogi when I have patience, which is not often.
B: Pierogi is like dumpling?
